assumptions.description: Oh Table 1 mean/SD and Table 2 TG levels are provisionally interpreted as arithmetic mg/dL summaries; Table 3 coefficient provisionally mg/dL per BMI. General geometric-average/log statement is unresolved, not silently ignored.

Transport Korean untreated family/twin relationships and US older healthy trial-volunteer female evidence to US adults. Fasting >=12 vs >=8 hours and plasma vs target serum are treated as comparable without a measured conversion. No population-specific offset is identified.

Conditional TG is lognormal with mean on arithmetic scale and sex-specific constant log residual SD; independent residual draws absorb omitted metabolic, behavioral, treatment and family factors. No residual family linkage is known for target.

Female age pattern is approximated by a smooth midlife rise from marginal Oh age strata, with midpoint50,width4,amplitude60 mg/dL and baseline logistic value .32; male modest slope -.3 mg/dL/year. These are conditional modeling assumptions because age-BMI joint dependence and confounding are unknown. Age response flat beyond20-80.

Conditional arithmetic BMI slopes are8.0 men/5.0 women after the single source-feedback revision. These are rounded assumptions, not published sex-specific adjusted slopes or causal effects. Oh pooled slope6.813 remains a diagnostic rather than an exact constraint. Above BMI35, effectiveBMI=35+10*log(1+(BMI-35)/10); this extreme-range extension remains unidentified.
Source-sex mean anchors rounded to142 and97 mg/dL and centered at published sex-specific BMI means. No recentering to target or generated-sample moments; not all source estimates are exactly fitted.

Conditional residual log SD=.65 men/.50 women. Initial .65/.48 was informed by Oh marginal CVs and expected covariate variation. Female .50 is a modest compensating assumption after reducing its BMI contribution, not a new reported estimate or exact variance fit. Bansal median/IQR supports right skew qualitatively; no formal pooling or calibrated parameter uncertainty.

Conditional arithmetic mean uses20+10*log(1+exp((linearMean-20)/10)) for positivity. Floor/softness are assumptions affecting low predictions; outcomes themselves are untruncated lognormal positive draws.

Oh source covariates use independent truncated normals within sex, based on Table1 mean/SD: ages20-79 rounded, BMI16-40. Rejection changes marginal moments; tails, distributional shapes, unknown age-BMI dependence, medication exclusions and family dependence are not reconstructed. Sex counts are8 times reported, only to reduce Monte Carlo noise.

WHS source covariates: all women; age45+Gamma with moments9.5 and7.2, rounded/clipped45-100; BMI lognormal with arithmetic mean25.9 SD5.0; independent age and BMI. Unreported joint structure, trial selection, medications and hormone use are not represented.16000 synthetic rows are Monte Carlo integration, not evidence.

Source integer TG categories are applied literally to continuous generated TG, including91-147; gaps between90/91 and147/148 are not reassigned. This rounding approximation can change proportions. Oh BMI intervals assigned [20,23),[23,25),[25,30],>30; endpoints are ambiguous in article.
Seeds vary only individual residual noise. Evidence interpretation, parameter uncertainty, model selection, unobserved confounding and transport uncertainty are not calibrated or sampled.

Verified initial source replay showed coherent female BMI association discrepancies across Oh extreme-BMI strata and Bansal BMI means by TG category, with opposite male direction in Oh. Use one partial, rounded sex interaction revision. Source age-BMI dependence, selection and effect heterogeneity remain unknown; this change may absorb their misspecification. No optimization, additional seed, target feedback, or claim of identified conditional effects.

model_family.derivation: Right skew and positive support motivate lognormal residuals; not proof of lognormality.

column_map.derivation: Task names and male code1; female2.

mean_anchor.derivation: Round141.6 to142 and97.2 to97; conditional-mean anchors, not fitted sample means.

bmi_reference.derivation: Published BMI centers; fixed for all contexts.

bmi_response.derivation: Initial common6.8 is revised once to rounded male8.0/female5.0 using the directional source-only diagnostic pattern bound in feedback/initial_source_replay.json. These are partial changes, not fitted source-specific slopes. Keep bend35/scale10 unchanged. The evidence does not identify age-adjusted sex-specific effects.

age_response.derivation: Smooth approximation of sex-specific marginal age shapes; no rank-to-Pearson conversion or claim of identified conditional effects.

positive_mean.derivation: Smooth positive extension with floor20 and softness10 mg/dL.

residual_log_sd.derivation: Oh marginal lognormal-equivalent log SD sqrt(log(1+(SD/mean)^2)) is about.68 men/.58 women. Keep male conditional.65; revise female.48 to.50 as a modest compensation for less BMI-driven variance. Feedback showed initial female marginal SD60.80 versus61.0, but no exact moment matching or optimization is performed. Conditional residual spread remains assumed.

source_recipe.derivation: Fixed source-only covariate recipes. Gamma age shape=((54.5-45)/7.2)^2,scale=7.2^2/(54.5-45); lognormal BMI from arithmetic moments. No TG generated or input.

uncertainty_mode.derivation: No target outcome or requested favorable result conditions this construction.
